sections.h2: Who sends the Carrollton property tax bill
sections.html:
A county tax office does, and which one depends on where your house sits, because Carrollton lies in Dallas, Denton and Collin counties. The Dallas County Tax Office bills Dallas County parcels, and the Denton County Tax Office bills parcels in both Denton and Collin counties. Statements go out in October, and they do not come from the City of Carrollton.

Value is set separately. The Dallas, Denton and Collin central appraisal districts each value the parcels in their county and hear protests. If you are unsure which county holds your lot, check the property address on an old statement or use the appraisal district search.

For fiscal year 2027, which began October 1, the City Council adopted a city rate of $0.537000 per $100 of assessed value. The city's news release calls it the lowest rate since 1989 and the 13th straight annual cut, down from $0.537500. The city also kept its senior and disabled exemptions at $110,000.

The average homestead market value is $419,401 and the average taxable value is $339,580, with the 20 percent homestead exemption and value caps applied. The city is one line among several. School, county and special-district rates stack on top, and the fiscal 2026 figures are below.

Three school districts serve Carrollton: Carrollton-Farmers Branch, Lewisville and Dallas ISD. Collin County's rate is not in this list, so a Collin-side owner should call the Denton County Tax Office or the Collin Central Appraisal District.

For the average Carrollton homestead, each dollar of property tax splits like this: $0.59 to the school district, $0.30 to the city and $0.11 to the county. The school share funds schools and operations. The city share pays for police, fire, streets, the library, parks, development, environmental work and animal control. The county share covers county roads, sheriff services, courts and health and human services.

The tax rate has two parts, maintenance and operations plus debt, and the Council sets it with the budget in August. A separate stormwater fee began October 1, 2026 on utility bills. About 80 percent of residential properties land in Tier 2 at $7.25. It is a utility charge, not a property tax.

The bill is payable starting October 1. Miss January 31 and it is delinquent. From there the cost climbs:

  • A 6% penalty starts in the first month of delinquency and grows 1% a month to reach 12% on July 1
  • Interest of 1% at the start, then 1% more each month
  • A further collection penalty of up to 20% of the taxes, penalties and interest, if the tax is still open on July 1

One alternative is paying in halves: half by November 30 and half by June 30, with a written request to waive penalty and interest. Owners 65 or older, or disabled, may spread payment over four installments. Confirm with the county tax office that you qualify before relying on either.

Send payment to whichever county office bills your parcel. Both take mail, online and in-person payments.

  • Dallas County parcels: mail to the Dallas County Tax Assessor-Collector, 500 Elm St., Dallas, TX 75202, or pay in person at the North Dallas location, 6820 LBJ Freeway, Suite 1300, Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Phone 214-653-7811.
  • Denton and Collin parcels: mail to the Denton County Tax Assessor-Collector, 1505 E. McKinney Street, Denton, TX 76209-4525, or pay in person at the Carrollton location, 1029 W. Rosemeade Parkway, Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Phone 940-349-3500.
  • Online payments carry fees, and both offices accept cards and echeck.

sections.h2: How to lower a Carrollton tax bill
sections.html:
File for every exemption you qualify for, and protest the value if you think it is too high. The city offers a 20 percent homestead exemption, a $110,000 exemption for owners 65 or older, a $110,000 exemption for disabled persons and and a disabled-veteran exemption. Applications go to the appraisal district, never to the city. A filing made by May 1 shows up on the original statement, and a later one generates a supplemental bill.

Every school district grants a $140,000 residence homestead exemption, with another $60,000 for homeowners who are 65 or older or disabled. To protest a value, file by May 15, or by the 30th day after the notice reaches you if that falls later. Appraisal notices usually arrive in April, and the appraisal district, not the city, hears the case.

sections.h2: Selling with this year's tax unpaid
sections.html:
The lien for a given year attaches on January 1, when value and ownership are also set. Yet the bill itself does not arrive until October, well after many spring and summer sales close. At closing, the agent should show how that year's tax is divided between you and the buyer.

Back taxes keep accruing penalties until July 1. Have the title company request an exact payoff from the county tax office. An old statement will be wrong, because the penalty and interest change every month.

A cash buyer usually pays these off from the proceeds at closing, so owing taxes does not by itself block a sale. What matters is that the payoff figure is current. Gather your most recent statement, your parcel number and the name of the county office before you call, and ask for the amount good through your expected closing date.

Owners who plan to sell should gather their latest tax statement from the county that bills the parcel, plus any exemption approval letters, before listing. A buyer's title company will ask which county the lot is in, whether a homestead exemption is on file, and whether any tax for earlier years is still open. Having those answers ready shortens the first week of escrow.

Carrollton had 134,562 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up from 133,434 in 2020, on 36.66 square miles. Owners occupy 58.5% of 51,995 households. Median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024 is $381,000, and median gross rent is $1,735. That survey median differs from the city's $419,401 average homestead market value, so the two figures will not match.

faqs.q: Which county tax office do I pay if my house is in Carrollton?
faqs.a: That depends on which county holds your parcel. Dallas County lots are billed by the Dallas County Tax Office, and Denton or Collin County lots by the Denton County Tax Office.

faqs.q: What is the Carrollton city property tax rate for fiscal year 2027?
faqs.a: $0.537000 per $100 of assessed value, lowered from $0.537500. The city calls it the lowest rate since 1989. School, county and special district rates are added on top.

faqs.q: When do Carrollton property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: After January 31. Taxes are payable from October 1, and a 6% penalty plus 1% interest start the month after the deadline. The penalty reaches 12% on July 1.

faqs.q: Does the City of Carrollton handle appraisal protests?
faqs.a: No. The Dallas, Denton and Collin central appraisal districts hear protests and approve exemptions. The filing deadline is May 15 or 30 days after the notice arrives, whichever is later.
Homestead (20 percent), age 65 or older ($110,000), disabled person ($110,000) and disabled-veteran. Apply through your county's appraisal district.
